Univariate Analysis¶

In [16]:
plt.figure(figsize=(8,5))
sns.countplot(x="Channel",data=df)
plt.title("Distribution of Marketing Channels")
plt.xlabel("Marketing Channel")
plt.ylabel("count")
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.show()

Interpretation¶

- Marketing campaigns are evenly distributed across all channels.¶

- No single channel dominates the dataset.¶

- This balanced distribution makes the data fair for comparison and analysis¶

In [17]:
plt.figure(figsize=(8,5))
sns.histplot(df["Impressions"],bins=30,)
plt.title("Distribution of Impressions")
plt.xlabel("Impressions")
plt.ylabel("Frequency")
plt.show()

Interpretation¶

- The histogram shows the distribution of Impressions across all campaigns.¶

- Impressions are fairly evenly distributed.¶

- No single impression range has a significantly higher frequency.¶

- This indicates a balanced campaign reach.¶

- Only a few campaigns generated very high clicks.¶

- The distribution is positively skewed,indicating that high click campaigns are less common.¶

Multivariate Analysis¶

In [28]:
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.heatmap(df.corr(numeric_only=True),annot=True,cmap="Purples")
plt.title("Correlation Heatmap")
plt.show()

Interpretation¶

- Impressions,Clicks,Leads,and Conversions show a strong positive relationship,meaning they increase together.¶

- Leads and Convertions have the strongest correlation (0.92),indicating that more leads usually result in more conversions.¶

- Cost and Revenue also have a strong positive correlation(0.86),suggesting that higher campaign spending generally generates higher revenue.¶

- ROI has only a moderate relationship with Revenue (0.44) and a weak relationship with the other variables.¶

In [29]:
sns.pairplot(df[["Impressions",
                 "Clicks",
                 "Conversions",
                 "Revenue_USD"]])
plt.show()

Interpretation¶

- The pair plot compares multiple numerical variable together.¶

- Impressions,Clicks,and Conversions show a positive relationship.As impression increases,clicks¶

and conversion also tend to increase.¶

- Revenue does not have a strong relationship with the other variables.Higher impressions,clicks¶

or conversions do not always result in higher revenue.¶

- The diagonal histogram show the distribution of each variables.Most observations are concentrated¶

at lower values,especially for clicks,conversions,and revenue.¶

- The scatter plots show a wide spread of data points.This indicates that the relationship between¶

some variables is not very strong.¶

- overall,customer engagement follows a positive trend ,while Revenue appears to be influanced by additional factors.¶

In [30]:
plt.figure(figsize=(8,5))
sns.scatterplot(x="Cost_USD",
                y="Revenue_USD",
                hue="Channel",
                data=df)
plt.title("Cost vs Revenue by Channel")
plt.xlabel("Cost(USD)")
plt.ylabel("Revenue(USD)")
plt.show()

Interpretation¶

- Cost and Revenue show a positive relationship.As campaign cost increases,revenue also tends to increase.¶

- All marketing channels follow a similar trend.No single channel clearly outperforms the others.¶

- The data points are widely spread.This suggests that revenue is influenced by factors other than cost.¶

- overall,higher campaign spending generally leads to higher revenue,regardless of the marketing channel.¶

Conclusion¶

The marketing campaign analysis provides valuable insights into the factors that influence campaign performance and business growth. The analysis shows that higher impressions, clicks, leads, and conversions are associated with better marketing outcomes, highlighting the importance of customer engagement. A strong positive relationship between campaign cost and revenue indicates that well-planned marketing investments can generate higher returns.¶

The visualizations and correlation analysis also demonstrate the value of data-driven decision-making in marketing. By continuously monitoring campaign performance, identifying customer behavior, and optimizing marketing strategies, businesses can improve their return on investment (ROI). Overall, the findings suggest that successful marketing campaigns depend not only on higher spending but also on effective planning, audience targeting, and continuous performance improvement, helping organizations achieve sustainable business growth.¶
